messages.subject: Some questions on FIELDImageR
parts:
Hello Dear Dr Filipe

I'm Evrard from Bénin Republic(West-Africa)

First of all let me congratulate you for the amazing work you've been doing on the package FIELDImageR project

I have use it and find some difficulties and I would know if there is a way to solve them.

1-The package doesn't come in R studio from internet?

2-Counting is easy with align species with the package but what if I'm in real situation with unaligned tree species, how can I train the model to know the species that i'm working on?

3-Is there anyway to count multiple tree species at a time or should I do it one by one if the problem at 2- is solved?

4-Using the DSM0 is easy when dealing with plant or horticultural species, but what if we are dealing with tree that have been there before drone image collection, is there any way to remove the vegetation so we have the soil only?

my email adress is akpla...@gmail.com. If I can have the pdf/latex/PPT files of some of the  documents, that can help me.

Thank you very much.

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Some questions on FIELDImageR
parts:
Hi Evrard,

Thank you for asking. 

I will try to answer your questions, but I appreciate some help to complement those from other members in our community.
1-The package doesn't come in R studio from internet?

Answer: Yes, the package does not is installed by default in RStudio. You need to install FIELDimageR in your computer by following one of the options available here: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#Instal
2-Counting is easy with align species with the package but what if I'm in real situation with unaligned tree species, how can I train the model to know the species that i'm working on?

Answer: The algorithm used in function fieldCount is based on image segmentation followed by the pixels distance matrix evaluation. We do not train a model in this strategy (it is not a machine learning method). To use this function and get good results it is important keep in mind that the objects (trees) should not touch each other, which it is super hard in natural landscapes as yours. The only way to get better results is if you choose/create a vegetation index that allows better separation among trees during the remove soil step (function fieldMask).
3-Is there anyway to count multiple tree species at a time or should I do it one by one if the problem at 2- is solved?

Answer: Following the answer above at question 2. You can select specific vegetation index and thresholding to identify each specie in your field (fieldMask and fieldIndex functions). And stead count the number of plants, you can use the function fieldArea to evaluate the percentage covered by each specie. Similar to what I did with different colors of seeds in this example here https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P8 , but in your case are different species.

4-Using the DSM0 is easy when dealing with plant or horticultural species, but what if we are dealing with tree that have been there before drone image collection, is there any way to remove the vegetation so we have the soil only?

Answer: One possible solution is to use the file called DTM (Digital Terrain Model) as soil base and the file DSM (Digital Surface Model) as trees coverage. The Canopy Height Model is calculated by CHM=DSM-DTM. Better explanation about differences between these files is on minute 45 of this video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U-bsA7QjzYE&t=1116s. The pipeline how to use FIELDimageR to calculate and extract CHP is available here https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P10 . 

 

Please, let me know if you have any other question and if the answers above helped you…!

All the best,

Filipe
